positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter believes generative AI is currently too unreliable for any healthcare use, citing frequent hallucinated or inaccurate outputs, and also raises concerns about protection of personal privacy. They express a preference for trained human clinicians providing care and health monitoring rather than AI devices.
positions.requested_fda_action: The comment does not specify a regulatory mechanism; it conveys general opposition to the use of generative AI in healthcare at this time, implying FDA should not permit such uses until accuracy and privacy concerns are resolved.
positions.public_summary: An individual commenter opposes current healthcare use of generative AI, citing hallucinated or inaccurate outputs and privacy risks, and states a preference for trained human clinicians providing care and health monitoring. The comment does not address FDA's specific framework questions.
positions.source_passage: Using generative AI for any healthcare usage at the moment is too risky, both in terms of accuracy (so much hallucinating going on), and in terms of protecting my privacy. I want trained human minds caring for me and monitoring my health, not some flaws hallucinating AI device.
